note: Real-time = can a continuous 50 kHz stream of non-overlapping 1024-sample windows be kept up with. Based on repository source-of-truth config; measurements are existing + this multiclass run. No new benchmark was run.

source_of_truth.on_chip_aggregation: 1024->256 (factor 4, after windowing; does not change window arrival rate)

level2_end_to_end.this_run_wall_note: wall throughput (0.569/s) includes gzip sequential-skip overhead: class_balanced indices are scattered across the 95404-window file, so the on-board runner decompresses up to tens of thousands of records to reach far indices. It is NOT an inference-rate measurement. The inference rate is reflected by per-window latency (mean 16.15 ms -> 61.9 inf/s core/DMA) and by the contiguous full-test sustained 46.4 inf/s.

verdict.fpga_core: REAL-TIME CAPABLE: 61.9 inf/s core vs 48.83 required (+26.8%); 16.15 ms latency vs 20.48 ms window period (+21% headroom).
verdict.end_to_end_current_demo: NOT real-time sustained on the current SSH/gz demo path: full-test 46.4 inf/s is 5.0% below required (shortfall 2.43/s); live SSH/UI 38.9 inf/s is ~20.3% below.
verdict.bottleneck: host/SSH per-window streaming + on-board Python loop + gzip input read -- NOT the inference core. A direct sensor->DDR->AXI-DMA feed (no gzip, no per-window SSH) is expected to close the ~5% gap because the core itself has margin.
verdict.honest_scope: Validated on PREPARED dataset windows, not a live 50 kHz sensor. 'Real-time' is a capacity statement under the configured stream, not a sensor-generalization claim.
